title: Glock wins a wet Hockenheim finale as BMW takes the manufacturers' title
dek: Timo Glock won his first DTM race, 2.787 seconds ahead of Roberto Merhi, after a long first stint on wet tyres in a rain-affected finale.

chapters.title: A champion crowned, three titles still to settle
text: The 2013 DTM season ended at Hockenheim on Sunday 20 October, three weeks after Zandvoort, where Mike Rockenfeller had finished second behind Augusto Farfus to become champion with a race to spare. His 142 points could no longer be reached, and Farfus, on 116, was already assured of second place. It was also the BMW M3's last outing in the series.

That left the other prizes to settle. Christian Vietoris was third in the standings on 71 points, but only one point ahead of Robert Wickens, with Gary Paffett and Bruno Spengler on 67 each, so the fight for third place was tightly bunched. In the team standings Audi Sport Team Phoenix led by three points from BMW Team RBM and by ten from the best Mercedes team, while Audi's lead over BMW in the manufacturers' table was under ten points.

Audi said it was going to Hockenheim aiming to add the team and manufacturers' titles to Rockenfeller's drivers' crown, while BMW needed its drivers in the points to turn the manufacturers' table around. With two mandatory stops in the race, the timing of the tyre changes would again shape the order, and a changeable track would make those calls harder.

chapters.title: Spengler leads a BMW top four
text: Bruno Spengler took pole position with a 1:33.443, 0.303 seconds faster than his Schnitzer team-mate Dirk Werner, who set 1:33.746. Andy Priaulx made the top three for BMW Team RMG with a 1:34.081, and Timo Glock took fourth for BMW Team MTEK, which gave BMW the first four places on the grid on the M3's final weekend.

Miguel Molina was the best Audi in fifth, ahead of Marco Wittmann in sixth, and Mattias Ekström and Adrien Tambay in seventh and eighth. Rockenfeller was ninth and Farfus tenth, with Martin Tomczyk 11th and Timo Scheider 12th. The Mercedes drivers fared badly: Wickens was the best in 13th, Paffett was 16th, and Vietoris 20th.
Further back, Albuquerque qualified 14th and Wehrlein 15th, with Juncadella 17th, Mortara 18th and Green 19th. Vietoris was 20th, Merhi 21st, and Joey Hand shared the back row in 22nd.

chapters.title: Glock stumbles, then hits Farfus
text: The race began in the rain. Spengler held the lead into the first corner, while Priaulx made an excellent start to run second ahead of Molina. Glock got a lot of wheelspin from fourth on the grid and lost places, then made contact with Farfus at the second corner. Farfus, who had gone from tenth to fifth, spun and dropped well down the field. Glock later apologised, saying he had been squeezed out under braking and had ended up on the slippery white line.

Albuquerque ran into trouble on the opening lap when he touched Wickens and had to stop. Merhi, last but one on the grid, jumped the start and served a drive-through penalty in the opening laps, though he soon showed he had the pace to climb back through the field. Meanwhile Glock passed Molina and Werner, then Priaulx, and moved up to second behind Spengler.

chapters.title: Spengler stops on lap 14, Glock stays out
text: Spengler made his first stop on lap 14 for fresh tyres and Glock inherited the lead. The earlier stop proved to be the decisive one: the race was drying, and the drivers who delayed their stops ran the quickest laps on the oldest tyres. Glock stayed out for roughly 30 laps on a single set of wets, and Ekström and Juncadella, who also ran long first stints, were closing on him as the track came back.

At the hairpin on lap 27 Juncadella made contact with Ekström and spun the Audi, which cost Ekström the chance to win. Juncadella was given a drive-through penalty and finished 10th. Ekström recovered to finish fourth.

chapters.title: Tomczyk and Hand gamble on slicks as Glock retakes the lead
text: Tomczyk and Hand were the first to try the dry-weather option tyre on lap 28, and both lost around seven to eight seconds a lap compared with the cars on wets, so they finished 19th and 20th, Hand a lap down. Rockenfeller also changed to slicks at his last stop and finished 16th, out of the points for the first time that season.

Merhi and Glock stopped on laps 30 and 31 and went back onto wet tyres. Merhi inherited the lead, but Glock, on fresher tyres, passed him at the hairpin with about six laps remaining and then pulled away. Merhi struggled for grip on his new set of wets and returned to the pits for his last stop, then matched Glock's pace over the final laps. Glock made his second stop shortly after, and kept the lead.

chapters.title: Glock wins by 2.787s; Spengler holds third
text: Glock took the flag after 41 laps in 1:16:44.053, 2.787 seconds ahead of Merhi, who had started 21st and recorded the best result of his DTM career. Spengler completed the podium, 10.120 seconds behind the winner, and held off Ekström, who was fourth at 11.365 seconds, after a late fight for third.

Molina was fifth, 15.619 seconds behind, and his result secured the team title for Phoenix Racing. Priaulx, who had run second at the wettest stage, was sixth, and Vietoris seventh, 30.466 seconds back, with the fastest lap of the race, a 1:46.908 on lap 39. Werner took eighth, Paffett ninth and Juncadella tenth, so those were the final points places.

Farfus fought back to 11th after his first-lap spin, and Green, Scheider and Tambay were 12th to 14th. Mortara was 15th and Rockenfeller 16th, while Wehrlein, Wickens, Tomczyk and Hand followed, Hand one lap down. Wittmann, who had started sixth, completed 37 laps and was disqualified, and Albuquerque did not get beyond the first lap.

chapters.title: BMW closes the M3 era with a first win for Glock
text: Glock's win was the first of his DTM career, in his tenth race, after a season in which his only previous podium was third place in Austria. He said the car had been very good all weekend and that the set-up changes made since Zandvoort had lifted it to a new level. He also made a point of apologising to Farfus, saying that contact between drivers of the same manufacturer should not happen. For BMW Team MTEK, a team that had not existed 11 months earlier, it was a first victory in its rookie year.

Merhi's second place from the back of the grid came close to a win. Mercedes' head of DTM management said the car had been the fastest in the rain, and that the aim for the winter was to have the same speed in the dry. Spengler, who had led early on, said the car's balance changed as the track dried in his second stint and he could not keep up with the leaders; his third place still lifted him to third in the final standings on 82 points. Marquardt, BMW's motorsport director, called the finale incredibly exciting and said Glock had shown strong nerves, and BMW's team principals pointed to a season that ended with the manufacturers' title, the unofficial rookie title for Wittmann and the award for the fastest pit crew, which went to Schnitzer.

The title fights ended as follows. Rockenfeller finished on 142 points, 26 ahead of Farfus on 116, with Spengler third on 82 and Vietoris, the best Mercedes driver, fourth on 77. Wickens ended on 70 and Paffett on 69. BMW won the manufacturers' title with 369 points, ahead of Audi, with Mercedes third on 266, while Phoenix took the team crown for Audi. BMW had won five races in 2013: Farfus three, Spengler one and Glock one.

For Rockenfeller, 16th in the finale was the first time that he had finished out of the points all year, but it cost him nothing. He called it a modest result. BMW bid farewell to the M3 with a win, and the series now moved into its winter break.

facts.v: Timo Glock won his tenth DTM race from fourth on the grid, 2.787 seconds ahead of Roberto Merhi, who had started 21st.
